mcps.name: Filesystem
mcps.description: Read and write files in configured directories on your computer.
mcps.instructions:
Enter the full paths of the directories you want the AI agent to access. Separate multiple paths with a space.

Example: /Users/you/Documents /Users/you/Desktop

The agent will only be able to read and write files inside these folders.

credentials_schema.label: Allowed Directories
credentials_schema.description: Space-separated full paths the agent can access.

mcps.name: Fetch
mcps.description: Make arbitrary HTTP requests and extract content from web pages.
mcps.instructions: No credentials required. Once installed this MCP is ready to use.

mcps.name: Memory
mcps.description: Persistent key-value memory store for the agent across runs.
mcps.instructions: No credentials required. Once installed the agent has a persistent memory store it can read and write across runs.

mcps.name: GitHub
mcps.description: Read and write GitHub issues, pull requests, repositories, and files.
mcps.instructions:
Create a Personal Access Token at github.com/settings/tokens.

Grant the repo scope (and read:org if you need organisation repositories). The token is stored securely in your OS keychain — never in any file.

mcps.name: Brave Search
mcps.description: Web and local search powered by the Brave Search API.
mcps.instructions:
Get a free API key at brave.com/search/api/

The key is stored securely in your OS keychain.

mcps.name: Slack
mcps.description: Read Slack channels, list messages, and post as a bot.
mcps.instructions:
Create a Slack app at api.slack.com/apps and install it to your workspace.

1. Go to api.slack.com/apps → Create New App
2. Add Bot Token Scopes: channels:read, chat:write, channels:history
3. Install to Workspace → copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...)
4. Find your Team ID in your Slack workspace URL (e.g. T012AB3CD)

Both values are stored securely in your OS keychain.

credentials_schema.label: Team ID
credentials_schema.description: e.g. T012AB3CD — found in your workspace URL

mcps.name: Notion
mcps.description: Read and edit Notion pages, databases, and blocks.
mcps.instructions:
Create an internal integration at notion.so/my-integrations.

1. Go to notion.so/my-integrations → New integration
2. Copy the Internal Integration Token
3. Share the Notion pages or databases you want the agent to access with that integration (Share → Invite → your integration name)

The token is stored securely in your OS keychain.
